heading: Gradient training can fit large convolutional networks to near-zero training error
definition: sufficiently large convolutional networks trained with SGD or Adam from random initialization reach zero or near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, including with corrupted or random labels; smaller models, early stopping and some regularized recipes leave substantial training error (Zhang et al. 2017; Nakkiran et al. 2020).
summary: Several independent groups reproduce zero or near-zero training classification error with SGD or Adam on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, including corrupted or random labels. Success depends on architecture, initialization and training recipe; smaller models, early stopping and some regularized recipes leave substantial training error.

suggested_status.by_scale: R2 at <1B for demonstrated CIFAR CNN recipes, including explicitly sized models in arXiv:2306.10947#R12 and arXiv:2306.10947#R13. versions.V1.studies_by_size contains <1B and not stated; other scale buckets are unassessed.
suggested_status.reason: Non-original supporting records reproduce fitting across architectures and recipes: SGD-trained CIFAR-10 Inception reaches 100.0% random-label training accuracy under a schedule selected for interpolation (arXiv:2306.10947#R5), while standard-initialized Adam CNNs explicitly interpolate clean CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 (arXiv:2402.15555#R1, arXiv:2402.15555#R2). This supports R2 for demonstrated recipes. Size alone is insufficient: original sigmoid VGG variants collapse to 10% training accuracy (arXiv:1809.10749#R1, arXiv:1809.10749#R5, arXiv:1809.10749#R9), and the tested He-initialized stripped ResNet fails with SGD (arXiv:2106.03763#R2, arXiv:2106.03763#R3, arXiv:2106.03763#R4). counts.json versions.V1.verdicts records supports alongside limits_scope and challenges; these condition-specific failures qualify the broad wording.
suggested_status.open_questions: Matched-recipe independent failures after adequate training would motivate C. Fully randomized-label Adam experiments on both CIFAR datasets would close the optimizer-by-label gap. A specified near-zero tolerance and endpoint convention would make replication outcomes comparable.

source.title: Understanding deep learning requires rethinking generalization
source.authors: Chiyuan Zhang; Samy Bengio; Moritz Hardt; B. Recht; O. Vinyals

original_result.setup: Zhang et al. trained Inception and Alexnet with SGD on CIFAR-10 using true, partially corrupted and random labels.
original_result.result: Inception and Alexnet reached 100.0% training accuracy on true and random labels without random cropping or weight decay, and Inception perfectly fit every tested partial-corruption level. Alexnet failed to converge on random labels with default weight decay.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Adam training on fixed, fully randomized CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100 labels.
untested.basis: Across the packs, explicit fully random-label CIFAR fitting uses SGD: arXiv:2105.02375#R2 (Section 4.2) and arXiv:2505.13142#R1. arXiv:2105.02375 Section 4.1 compares Adam, SGD and LBFGS on unmodified datasets; no fully random-label Adam experiment is reported. arXiv:2402.15555#R1, arXiv:2402.15555#R2 and arXiv:2402.15555#R3 concern clean-label Adam interpolation. arXiv:1912.02292#R1 and arXiv:1912.02292#R2 use Adam on CIFAR-10 with 15% label noise; arXiv:1912.02292#R3 uses Adam on CIFAR-100 with varying label noise including none. Section 4 states that corrupted labels are sampled once and retained across epochs. No fully randomized-label Adam experiment is reported there; fully randomized labels are not explicitly excluded. counts.json versions.V1.coverage_by_operation and versions.V1.main_rows_by_operation aggregate operations without optimizer-by-label coverage; these keys do not establish the missing combination.

wording_issues.issue: Size alone does not specify successful fitting. Original sigmoid VGG11/13/16 collapse to 10% CIFAR-10 training accuracy; a 500-layer He-initialized stripped ResNet fails under tested SGD settings. The CIFAR-10 convolutional capacity sweep combines size with plateau stopping; its R7 result is partial fitting at 43.82% training accuracy and 56.18% training error, supporting the smaller-model qualification rather than exhibiting near-zero error. Model-zoo maxima aggregate widths and batch sizes without identifying successful configurations.

The initialization distribution, phase and scale matter. Nonnegative, same-variance initialization prevents batch-normalized VGG19 and ResNet50 from fitting within the displayed budgets. On 1,000 CIFAR-10 examples, CNN-F shows depth-dependent degradation in sufficiently deep ordered-phase configurations; remaining training error is unquantified. CIFAR-10 ResNet-56/110 runs use low-rate SGD, batch size 128, and a maximum 300-epoch cosine schedule with early stopping, patience 30. Over 10 seeds, final training accuracy at σw=2.5 versus 0.1 is 60.7±1.3% versus 81.9±11.0% for ResNet-56 and 60.2±1.6% versus 76.6±8.7% for ResNet-110. These endpoints do not establish eventual nonconvergence.

Some fitting evidence extends beyond the named optimizers: completed, nondivergent VGG10 runs use full-batch GD with a >99.99% training-accuracy completion criterion; tanh CNNs use RMSprop; random-label convolutional fitting uses Entropy-SGLD; and modified ResNets use LAMB. Full-batch GD is optimizer-extension evidence, with cannot_determine for literal V1 and no V1 version link. For the Entropy-SGLD sweep at β=1, sufficiently large τ gives almost-zero training classification error, while small τ suppresses fitting; the transition depends on γ. These outcomes need their optimizer labels when presented alongside direct SGD/Adam evidence.

wording_issues.phrase: trained with SGD or Adam from random initialization
wording_issues.issue: Supporting endpoints do not always establish the complete recipe. SWA refinement and rank manipulations continue from trained weights. The SGD ResNet-18 interpolation statement leaves initialization unspecified. Clean-label Adam interpolation on both CIFAR datasets is explicitly supported, but its numerical training-accuracy endpoints are unavailable.

wording_issues.phrase: including with corrupted or random labels
wording_issues.issue: Dataset, optimizer and label regime should remain explicit. Row-backed fully random-label SGD fitting includes CIFAR-10 VGG/ResNet experiments. CIFAR-100 evidence includes eventual memorization with 20% uniform noise and near-complete baseline VGG-11 fitting of clean and noisy subsets with 25% corruption. Clean-label Adam interpolation does not establish all optimizer-by-dataset-by-label combinations.

wording_issues.phrase: reach zero or near-zero training classification error
wording_issues.issue: No common near-zero tolerance or endpoint convention is supplied. VGG-16 verdicts accept 0.3% and 0.11% error as near-zero. For CIFAR10, R=1, rho=0.5, n=25250, the imbalance study uses ResNet-18 and VGG-13 with batch normalization replacing dropout; its zero-error criterion permits 0.2% majority error, and the 0.00% minority-error requirement applies when nmin<=500. Perfect PreResNet32 accuracy is transient. Full-batch GD completion means >99.99% training accuracy for completed, nondivergent VGG10/CIFAR10-5k, VGG19/CIFAR10-50k, VGG19/CIFAR10-500k and ResNet20/CIFAR10-500k runs. Those results establish neither an unconditional success rate nor literal V1's SGD/Adam fitting claim; they are optimizer-extension evidence.

The evidence mixes direct classification measurements and other endpoints. ResNet18's nearly zero cross-entropy loss supports an inferred classification outcome. The binary ResNet-20 result is squared loss, with a classification bound supplied by the verdict. BN-LeNet measures noisy-subset loss. VGG19_BN's plotted Mixup accuracy differs from its separately stated original-set interpolation.

Some evidence concerns restricted tasks or evaluated subsets. CNN-F uses 1,000 CIFAR-10 examples; separate convolutional experiments use 100 examples; the VGGNet experiment uses binary CIFAR-10. Cyclic-batching accuracy is evaluated on a 5,000-example training subset, leaving complete-training-set classification error unmeasured in that study.

The qualification is dataset- and recipe-dependent. Small Conv2FC1 retains 12.82% training error. In the CIFAR-10 convolutional size sweep, R7 has 43.82% training accuracy and 56.18% error, while R10 has 97.65% accuracy and 2.35% error; both exhibit partial fitting, compared with 99.84%–100.0% accuracy in larger reported models. That sweep combines capacity with stopping. These partial outcomes support V1's smaller-model qualification. Conversely, narrow ResNet-10 attains perfect evaluated training-subset accuracy under uniform batching, and the smallest tested MNIST sigmoid CNNs already have near-zero error.

wording_issues.phrase: early stopping and some regularized recipes leave substantial training error
wording_issues.issue: Stopping procedures and regularization need their conditions. Instance-dependent sample exclusion still permits full-set interpolation. Short-budget AdamW training retains error, while a rowless verdict reports zero error with longer training. PGD outcomes depend on dataset, architecture and defensive strength; incomplete CIFAR-10 fitting for ResNet-56 at strengths 8/16 and ResNet-110 at strength 16 supports V1's existing regularized-recipe qualification rather than adding a scope limitation. Fisher Penalty also has architecture-dependent fitting effects. These results do not isolate a universal stopping or regularization effect.

method_sensitivity.factor: Learning rate, batch size and optimizer
method_sensitivity.what: CIFAR-100 VGG-16 reaches 99.7% or 99.89% training accuracy at batch size 1024 and learning rates 0.08 or 0.028. Training does not occur under SGD with batch size 4096, initial learning rate 0.32, no batch normalization and zero weight decay; no exact training-error value is stated. Sphere-constrained CIFAR-10 ConvNets reach zero error in converged low-effective-learning-rate runs but approximately 90% error at effective learning rate ≥ 2 × 10−2. SGD cannot train the tested 500-layer He-initialized stripped ResNet at learning rates 1e-3, 1e-6 or 1e-9. Binary-CIFAR MobileNet reaches its zero-loss endpoint only in convergent runs; excessive rates diverge.

method_sensitivity.factor: Initialization distribution, scale and residual-branch scaling
method_sensitivity.what: CNN-F networks fit perfectly in the deep chaotic initialization region; degradation is restricted to sufficiently deep ordered-phase configurations on 1,000 CIFAR-10 examples, with remaining training error unquantified. Nonnegative, same-variance initialization prevents BN VGG19 and ResNet50 from fitting within short displayed windows. Under low-rate SGD, ResNet-9 retains near-complete fitting across reported initialization extremes. On CIFAR-10, smaller ResNet-56/110 use a maximum 300-epoch cosine schedule with early stopping, patience 30: at σw=2.5 versus 0.1, final training accuracies are 60.7±1.3% versus 81.9±11.0% for ResNet-56 and 60.2±1.6% versus 76.6±8.7% for ResNet-110, over 10 seeds. Unnormalized residual-network sweeps include interpolation and scaling-dependent divergence; deeper failures are verdict-only.

Original sigmoid VGG11/13/16 collapse to 10% CIFAR-10 training accuracy, while output-skip SGD variants reach 100%; Appendix F specifies 1000 epochs for sigmoid skip-SGD, qualifying Section 4's nominal 300 epochs. Softplus VGG11 reaches 100%. In scaled CIFAR-10 residual networks, GELU training errors are 19.5% with weight-tied initialization and 10.2% with i.i.d. initialization; ReLU errors are 2.6% and 1.6%. Activation changes improve short, regularized CIFAR-100 PlainNet results without establishing interpolation. Five-epoch regularized AdamW RePU/MRePU recipes can learn, stall or overflow depending on activation, input kernel and residual configuration. Post-BN-γ-crit MRePU p=2 learns in all three seeds but fits partially, with training-accuracy fractions 0.70–0.71; two seeds finish at chance test accuracy.

The fixed-random-label CIFAR-10 CNN reaches 100.0% fitting accuracy with PLN[8], versus 95.8% with the best conventional GN domain and 24.6% with full-feature-map LN. Normalization supplies the intermediate nonlinearity in these comparisons. Separately, tested PCA-whitening configurations cause VGG training failure, and tested ZCA configurations other than ZCA-16 fail numerically. ZCA-16 and ItN train successfully, without readable final training-error endpoints.

method_sensitivity.factor: Training duration, schedules and loss adjustment
method_sensitivity.what: Instance-dependent stopping still permits full-set interpolation: CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 accuracy rises from 95.96% at epoch 50 to 99.99% at epoch 100 and 100.00% at epochs 150/200. Long-tailed CIFAR-10 ResNet-32 has approximately 93% accuracy with CDT and 97% with VS at epoch 200; longer training approaches 100%, while LA reaches 100%. On partially corrupted CIFAR-100, scheduler choice changes memorization timing. Under the small-CNN 1000-step AdamW budget, Constant, Cosine and Two-Point Spline give median training-error fractions of 0.118 ± 0.005, 0.0918 ± 0.001 and 0.0627 ± 0.001.

The CIFAR-10 convolutional size sweep shows partial fitting at 43.82% training accuracy (56.18% error) and 97.65% accuracy (2.35% error), compared with 99.84%–100.0% accuracy in larger models. This supports V1's smaller-model qualification; the shared loss/plateau stopping rule confounds capacity and stopping. Small Conv2FC1 remains below interpolation under its 400-epoch recipe. In dataset extensions, MNIST sigmoid-CNN errors fall from 8 to 1 to zero as filters increase from 10 to 20 to tested widths of at least 30; even the smallest tested model is near-zero. CelebA ResNet10 worst-group training error reaches zero as width increases from 1 to 96, from 12.4% at width 1, under the reweighted objective and weight decay λ=0.0001; initialization is unspecified.

method_sensitivity.factor: Explicit penalties, privacy noise and truncation
method_sensitivity.what: On 25%-corrupted CIFAR-100, Fisher Penalty leaves VGG-11 accuracy at 79.52% on clean examples and 4.10% on assigned noisy labels, versus baseline 99.79% and 99.56%. At β=1, Entropy-SGLD achieves almost-zero training classification error on random CIFAR-10 labels at sufficiently large τ; fitting is suppressed at small τ, with the transition depending on γ. Privacy/smoothing-constrained clean-CIFAR training retains approximately 6% error after prolonged training. Private WRN-40-4 CIFAR-10 accuracy rises from 51.2% to 81.5% across cumulative normalization, batch-size, weight-standardization, augmentation and averaging changes, remaining short of interpolation. Singular-value truncation changes two-layer BN CNN accuracy from 87.33% to 78.41% under 50-epoch AdamW training.

method_sensitivity.factor: Adversarial or sharpness-aware objectives and label subsets
method_sensitivity.what: Natural training fits the MNIST dataset with 15% randomized labels completely, whereas adversarial training leaves 997 errors, including 994 randomized-label examples. Increasing PGD strength lowers clean training accuracy for CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 ResNets, with residual error depending on depth and dataset. These regularized-recipe results support V1's stated recipe dependence. The SAM/SGD comparison distinguishes clean and noisy training examples and reports higher clean-example accuracy for SAM before noisy examples are fitted; unreadable endpoints leave final whole-set fitting unresolved.

method_sensitivity.factor: Augmentation, batch composition and evaluation set
method_sensitivity.what: WRN-28-10 reaches zero CIFAR-10 error without augmentation, whereas augmented simple-schedule runs do not reach exact zero after 200 epochs; the residual magnitude is unavailable. Uniform versus selected cyclic batching changes narrow ResNet-10 training-subset accuracy from 100.00 ± 0.00% to 94.65 ± 0.58%, while Myrtle5 and wider ResNet-10 retain perfect subset accuracy. VGG19_BN interpolation concerns the original training set, distinct from plotted Mixup accuracy. Original-source Alexnet fails to converge on random labels with default weight decay, while Inception fits in the cited unregularized run.

method_sensitivity.factor: Training stage, averaging and endpoint selection
method_sensitivity.what: On CIFAR-100, SWA versus subsequent SGD-refinement accuracies are 94.98% versus 97.52% for ResNet-110, 97.48% versus 99.12% for ResNet-164, and 99.84% versus 99.87% for DenseNet-100. PreResNet32 full-batch training reaches transient perfect accuracy rather than maintaining it. As optimizer-extension coverage, the stability study defines completion as >99.99% training accuracy for completed, nondivergent VGG10/19 and ResNet20 full-batch GD runs; these do not directly test V1's SGD/Adam recipe (state cannot_determine; version link none). Random-label CIFAR-10 ResNet-20 fails to fit during its fifth cosine-annealing round after filter collapse. The plotted measure is training top-1 accuracy; the authors describe good fitting in the first four rounds, without numerical endpoints.
